Dining room furnished in parts/room-6.mjs: oak-slab table on oak-fence legs with a red rug, oak-stair benches on the north and south sides, a barrel sideboard with flower pots on the east wall, and four hanging lanterns.
`./make.sh` writes a whole build.nbt with the part showing 40 placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines. `mcd room` says OK: 54/54 floor cells reachable, minimum light 8, no dim or dark cells.
The render was read: the table and benches read clearly from inside; the sideboard is hidden from the inside view. Rear windows and the doorway are clear.

waste.what: Worked out the floor-grid column and row mapping by hand (x 10..18 free, the x 9 wall, the z 15 and z 22 edges, which cells are windows) before drawing the layers.
waste.cost: about 4 minutes of reasoning and several re-reads of the plan grid
waste.tool: `mcd plan` could print a second grid of only the free interior cells, with absolute x/z labels on both axes, and mark which wall cells belong to the room box versus the shell.

waste.what: Light iteration by hand: placed lanterns, ran `mcd room`, read the dim-cell grid, then moved lanterns and rebuilt.
waste.cost: two make.sh runs and two room checks
waste.tool: `mcd room --suggest 8` could output a minimal set of hanging-lantern coordinates that clears every dim cell, so the designer does not have to infer them from the light grid.

waste.what: Table height trap: a candle cannot sit on a slab-top table because the slab fills the y 15 cell, so the centrepiece had to be lanterns instead of candles. I found this by reasoning, not by a check.
waste.tool: a furniture helper (`table(fence+slab)` in vocab, or a `layers` legend note) that states which cells a table occupies and where a tabletop item can go.

companions.task: Place the hanging lanterns and check the dim cells before the furniture went in, so the layout was not redone to fit the light.
Pick the rug and any cushions for the benches; I only had red carpet under the table.
